newsitem.title: USA: Gaidar says worst of Russia's problems over.
newsitem.headline: Gaidar says worst of Russia's problems over.

text.p: Former Acting Russian Prime Minister Yegor Gaidar said Friday that Russia is over the worst of its economic problems, but that a broad package of reforms addressing tax and spending issues was needed.
"I think now we have passed the most serious problems," Gaidar, one of Russia's early architects of economic reform, told a National Press Club gathering.

He said tax collections are starting to improve, but the government needed to reduce taxes on wages and make the system simpler and fairer. He also called for budget reforms that cut social welfare benefits to middle class people and focused those benefits on the poor.
Gaidar said President Boris Yeltsin needed to make a broad economic reform the centerpiece of his second term.

Tax collection has been a major problem in Russia, with a number of big corporations failing to make payments. The problems prompted the International Monetary Fund to delay paying the October tranche of a $10 billion loan to Russia.
But Gaidar said now that the presidential election is over and Yeltsin's health appears to be improving following his heart surgery, the tax collection situation is improving.
An IMF mission is currently in Russia to determine whether the money can be paid out.
